summary: The result of an operation, or an error the reader has to act on, as one message: a toast, a bar at the top of the content, or a line beside the control.
not_for: An input error, which sits beside its field (references/interaction.md, Feedback), or a question before an operation (feedback.confirm).

slots.when: The operation can be undone: 元に戻す.
The message stays until it is closed.

rules.rule: A message is one sentence that names what happened.
A message that stays until it is closed carries a control that closes it, and a timed one closes by itself after the time the conventions give.
The screen shows the number of messages the conventions give, and a new one takes the place of the oldest.
A message that must not interrupt the work is a toast, and one the reader has to act on stays where it happened.
The types are few and fixed: success, error, information.

maps_to.shadcn: MessageBar of the kit, or a Sonner toast

evidence.source: cybozu developer network, kintone JavaScript API, 通知を表示する
evidence.says: A notification at the top of the screen is one of three types (error, success, information), stays until it is closed, and shows one at a time: the last one called replaces the others.
A notification bar is hidden by an explicit action of the user; closing it after a time is discouraged.

evidence.source: Microsoft Learn, Power Apps client API, setFormNotification
evidence.says: A form notification stays visible until the code removes it.
A message toast closes by itself; its duration, 3000 ms by default, is the time before the close animation starts.

A message dialog interrupts the work by blocking the page until the user closes it; a message toast is for a less important message that must not block; messages have four types, each with its colour and icon.
